name: The Warsong Reports
summary: Kadrak sends couriers from the northern Barrens to gather reports across Ashenvale. The Warsong Reports carry orders and field observations from outriders near Azshara, Splintertree Post, and the Zoram Strand.

sections.title: Frontier Logistics
sections.body: Kadrak watches the mountain pass between the northern Barrens and Ashenvale from a fortified tower. The Horde needs the pass because the Barrens cannot supply the timber Orgrimmar requires. The Warsong clan has pushed into the ancient elven forest to reach those supplies. Couriers carry orders between scattered patrols and help keep them in step, while night elf ambushes threaten the wilderness trails.

sections.title: Eyes Across Ashenvale
sections.body: Warsong scouts watch three parts of Ashenvale. On the western coast, a runner at Zoram'gar Outpost watches naga activity and other coastal threats along the Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, a scout coordinates defense against Sentinel raids. Farther east, an outrider watches the road toward the shattered ruins of Azshara. Their reports give Kadrak a view of night elf movements and weaknesses along the frontier.

faq.answer: The reports begin with Kadrak, an orc officer in the wooden watchtower guarding the mountain pass between the northern Barrens and southern Ashenvale.

faq.q: Why is the Horde spying on Ashenvale?
faq.answer: The Horde seeks Ashenvale's dense timber to build and reinforce settlements such as Orgrimmar. Night elves fiercely defend their sacred groves, and constant scouting helps the Horde maintain its outposts and supply lines in the conflict.

faq.q: Where can the three Warsong scouts be found?
faq.answer: The Warsong Runner is at Zoram'gar Outpost on the far northwestern Zoram Strand. The Warsong Scout is at Splintertree Post along the main road. The Warsong Outrider patrols the eastern road toward Azshara's border.
Warsong outriders are scouts and raiders of the Warsong orc clan. Their cavalry and skirmishing help the Horde expand, harvest lumber, and defend territory in Ashenvale's forests.

faq.q: What happens after returning the reports?
faq.answer: When Kadrak receives the reports, he uses them to plan troop movements, reinforce vulnerable outposts such as Zoram'gar and Splintertree, and strengthen the Horde's presence deeper in the forest.

faq.q: Is the road through Ashenvale safe for low-level couriers?
faq.answer: No. Night elf Sentinels often ambush travelers on Ashenvale's main road. Prowlers, bears, and Alliance patrols from settlements such as Astranaar also threaten couriers.

angles.text: Delivering these reports gives a young Horde warrior an early role in the struggle against the night elves in northern Kalimdor.
For orcs, aiding the Warsong clan honors the clan and helps supply the lumber needed to build Orgrimmar.
As a hunter, you test your navigation and survival skills on Ashenvale's dangerous roads, where wild predators and hidden elven archers pose threats.
